archetype.name: Fringe Contender (offense-first)
archetype.definition: A 7-2 Detroit team whose top-tier passing offense and special teams have outrun a bottom-five defense, good enough to win a three-way division race but without the margin of a true Super Bowl favorite.

report.headline: An elite passing offense is carrying a leaky defense that just lost Hutchinson.
report.take:
Detroit is still built the way it has been through the Campbell era: an offense that wins on efficiency and a defense that tries to survive. Goff has started every game and thrown for 2437 yards, the passing offense ranks 5th in EPA, and the overall success rate ranks 3rd. Add a special-teams unit ranked 3rd and a coach who has gone for every fourth down he could (a 100% go rate, 1st), and you have a team that piles up points even on days the run game sputters. History says this is normal. Detroit's defense was 31st in EPA allowed in 2022 and 21st in 2023, and the only great season, 2024, came when the defense rose to 7th.

The 7-2 record flatters the team a bit. Net EPA is 0.018, 16th in the league, which is the profile of an average team on a down-to-down basis. The record sits 0.89 wins above what the point differential implies, and the Lions have won 0.8 of their one-score games, 3rd in the league. Last year the close games went the other way (0.375, 20th) and a team with similar efficiency finished 9-8. Turnovers aren't propping it up: the defense ranks 25th in takeaways. The wins have come from out-scoring people and holding on in tight games.

The defense is the story behind the box scores. It ranks 30th in EPA allowed and 27th against the pass, gives up conversions on third down (27th), and gets beaten underneath: short-pass EPA allowed ranks 27th, and lead tight ends have done damage against it (31st). Opponents pass on it more than almost anyone (2nd-strongest pass funnel), because the run defense is solid (8th in rush EPA) and the tackling is the cleanest in the league. What kept it afloat was the pass rush, 4th in sack rate and 5th in QB hit rate. In the four games since early October it held opponents to 17, 15, 9 and 10 points, though those offenses were mostly mediocre.

That's why the injury report matters more than the standings. Aidan Hutchinson tore his ACL against New England and is gone for the year, so the engine of that pass rush is out. Linebacker Jack Campbell (97% of snaps) is on IR until December, corner D.J. Reed (94%) is out, and Kerby Joseph hasn't played at all. A defense that was already relying on sacks to cover for coverage problems now has to win with fewer sacks and a thinner secondary. Detroit can still win the North on offense, but the margin for error just shrank.

strengths.title: A passing offense that rarely stalls
strengths.body: Goff and a target tree led by St. Brown (91 targets) with Williams, LaPorta and Gibbs behind him make the dropback game one of the league's most efficient. The line keeps him clean: its pressure rate allowed ranks 5th, so the passing game doesn't have to rely on quick throws to survive. It's the most stable piece of the roster and matches the 2023-25 track record.

strengths.title: Hidden points from special teams, aggression
strengths.body: Special teams add value nearly every week (3rd in EPA per game), and Campbell has gone on every fourth-down chance the model flags. Together they turn drives into points and help explain a scoring offense ranked 5th despite a middling run game. Both reflect coaching philosophy more than luck, so they should hold.

strengths.title: Sound run defense and tackling
strengths.body: The front stops the run well (8th in rush EPA allowed) and the league's lowest missed-tackle rate keeps short completions from becoming long gains. That part of the defense depends less on Hutchinson's pass rush and should travel into the second half.

concerns.title: Pass defense loses its cover
concerns.body: The coverage was already bad: 27th in pass EPA allowed, 27th on short throws, 31st against lead tight ends. A pass rush 4th in sack rate hid a lot of that, and Hutchinson's torn ACL takes away its best player while Reed and Campbell are also out. Expect more completed drives and more third downs converted until the rush finds another answer.

concerns.title: Record ahead of the efficiency
concerns.body: An average net EPA (16th) and a 0.8 win rate in one-score games are a mismatch, and the record sits nearly a full win above its point differential. Last season the same close-game coin flips broke the other way. With four division games left against teams at 6-4 or better, some of those tight wins probably become losses.

concerns.title: Run game too committed, not physical enough
concerns.body: Detroit runs more than the situation suggests (25th in pass rate over expected) even though its passing is far more efficient than its rushing. Gibbs has a strong success rate, but the line gets stuffed often (27th) and fails in short yardage (27th). With center Cade Mays out, that leaning on the run gets harder to justify.

trend.note: Shootouts early (30, 41, 24 and 32 allowed in the first four) gave way to a defense-led run of 17, 15, 9 and 10 allowed. Losing Hutchinson right at the end of that stretch makes it unlikely that defensive form holds as is.

nextGame.headline: Tampa's defense is better than 3-6; laying 6.5 is real work
nextGame.body:
Detroit is a 6.5-point home favorite indoors, but this matchup is closer than the records say. Tampa Bay is 3-6 with a positive point differential, a net EPA ranked 10th (ahead of Detroit's 16th) and a 0.143 record in one-score games, 30th. Its defense ranks 2nd in EPA allowed against both pass and run and leads the league in takeaways. The weak spots: it doesn't pressure the quarterback (30th in pressure rate), it misses tackles (29th), and deep throws and WR2s have hurt it. Its offense is the problem, 29th in EPA and 30th passing, leaning on a run game that averages 4.81 yards a carry and controls the clock.

Availability swings both sidelines. Baker Mayfield is questionable with a foot sprain; Jalon Daniels started three games in his place earlier, and Tampa's passing game would get even thinner without Mayfield. Safety Antoine Winfield Jr. is questionable and linebacker Yaya Diaby is out. For Detroit, this is the first game without Hutchinson, and Reed, Joseph and center Cade Mays are also out, with Jack Campbell on IR. The Lions' defense will have to win without the pass rush that carried it.

waysToWin.title: Clean pocket, push the ball deep
waysToWin.body: Tampa ranks 30th in pressure rate and Detroit's line allows little pressure, so Goff should have time. The Bucs smother WR1s and short throws but give ground deep and to the second receiver, which points the game plan toward Jameson Williams and downfield shots rather than force-feeding St. Brown.

waysToWin.title: Make Tampa throw
waysToWin.body: Tampa wants to run (30th in pass rate over expected) and is 30th in passing EPA, worse still if Mayfield can't go. Detroit's run defense ranks 8th; if it holds up early, a lead forces the Bucs into their weakness, behind a line that allows sacks at the 29th-ranked rate even with Hutchinson out.

waysToWin.title: Turn catches into extra yards
waysToWin.body: Tampa's defense is efficient but misses tackles at the 29th-ranked rate. Gibbs on screens and checkdowns, and LaPorta after the catch, can stretch modest gains against a unit that otherwise wins the down.

waysToLose.title: Feeding the takeaway machine
waysToLose.body: Tampa leads the league in takeaways, and that is how a 29th-ranked offense keeps games close. Detroit turned it over twice against Green Bay and New England; doing that here gives the Bucs short fields and hands them points their offense can't produce otherwise.

waysToLose.title: Stubborn run game, stalled drives
waysToLose.body: Tampa ranks 2nd in rush EPA allowed, and Detroit's line is stuffed often and loses short-yardage downs, now without Mays at center. If the Lions keep leaning on the run like they have all season, drives stall and the game turns into the low-scoring grind Tampa wants.

waysToLose.title: Bucs grind clock on depleted defense
waysToLose.body: Tampa's run game ranks 3rd in yards per carry and its offense ranks 3rd in time of possession. Facing a defense missing its best rusher, a starting corner and its top linebacker, long drives keep Goff on the sideline and turn this into a one-score game where Tampa's poor close-game luck could turn.

nextGame.watch: Detroit's pass rush in its first game without Hutchinson, against a Tampa line that allows sacks at a bottom-four rate, likely with a less-than-full-strength quarterback.

restOfSeason.body:
The offense is real and should keep Detroit near the top of the scoring ranks: passing efficiency, protection, special teams and fourth-down aggression have all held up across several seasons. What likely won't hold is the 0.8 one-score win rate and the defense's recent run of single-digit and mid-teens scores, which came against mostly weak offenses and relied on a pass rush that just lost Hutchinson. Expect points allowed to drift back toward the early-season level, with Campbell's return in December the main source of help.

The schedule turns the division into a three-way fight. Chicago twice and Minnesota on the road are games against 7-2 teams, Green Bay closes the year on the road, and Atlanta, Tennessee and the Giants are the gettable stretch. A team with average net EPA playing that slate should win a little more than half its remaining games. That still puts Detroit in the playoff picture, but the division title probably comes down to the Chicago games and whether the offense can win shootouts it used to win more comfortably.
swingFactors: Jack Campbell's return from IR in December
Two games with Chicago in the three-way division race

confidence.note: Nine games of stable offense, but the defense just lost three key starters at once.
